title: 1-Wire target: reset / presence, write slots assembling a byte (LSB first), then read slots returning a byte

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: Byte returned on the read slots after each byte received

fields.desc: taken when a byte's last write slot is sampled, then sent LSB first on the next 8 read slots

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Bytes written by the controller; reading RX frees it

fields.desc: between a reset pulse and the bus going idle (not cleared by the transfer ending: only the core's reset returns it to idle)

irqs.name: BYTE
irqs.desc: a byte was received (the same clock RX captures it)

notes: dq (open drain: the target only pulls it low) is the 1-Wire pin; it passes through unchanged. Timing is in units of US = 10 PCLK clocks per microsecond (the core parameter): a reset is more than 480 us low, the presence pulse follows 15 us after release for 120 us, write slots are sampled 30 us after their falling edge, a 0 read slot is held low for 40 us.

After a byte is received the target sends TX on the next 8 read slots, then waits for the next byte. A reset pulse at any point restarts with a presence pulse. ROM commands (Read ROM, Match ROM, Search ROM) are not implemented: every byte is data.
